anf_compare.notes: Translated from the PG 77 Greek. No published English version was used for wording.

choices.why: Honorific address ('your godliness'); the plural ὑμῶν addresses the bishops together. It stays the subject of περιεργαζέσθω and χειροτονείτω.
rejected: the bishop (supplies a subject the Greek lacks)

choices.why: Most likely from marital relations; the English keeps the Greek's reticence.

choices.term: εἰ μή τίς ἐστι τῶν ἐκβεβλημένων
choices.english: whether he is one of those who have been expelled
choices.why: Indirect question with μή: the check is for exclusion.
rejected: let him make sure that he is not (adds a verb)

choices.english: once he has been found blameless
choices.why: Aorist participle: the ordination follows the finding.

pass_a_gloss: (c) Concerning how and when it is necessary to ordain (cheirotoneō) and whom it is necessary to examine (exetazō). Since therefore all things must be done by us toward the building up (oikodomē), as I said, of the peoples, let your godliness (theosebeia) watch over (epitēreō) these things; and if anyone should be about to be ordained a cleric, let [your godliness] inquire closely into (periergazomai) his life (bios), both whether he ever has a wife (gametē) or not, and how or when he took [her] (agō), and whether he abstained (apechomai); and whether he is not one of those expelled (ekballō) either by another most God fearing (theosebestatos) bishop or from monasteries; and then let [your godliness] ordain, [him] having been found (heuriskō) blameless (adiablētos).
pass_b_english: 3. How and when one should ordain, and whom one should examine

Since, then, as I said, everything we do must be done for building up the people, let Your Reverence watch over these matters. If anyone is about to be ordained a cleric, let Your Reverence look carefully into his life: whether he has a wife or not, how or when he married her, and whether he has abstained; and whether he is one of those who have been expelled, either by another most God-fearing bishop or from monasteries. And then let Your Reverence ordain him, once he has been found blameless.
source_text:
(γ) Περὶ τοῦ πῶς καὶ πότε δεῖ χειροτονεῖν καὶ τίνα δεῖ ἐξετάζειν. Ἐπειδὴ
τοίνυν πρὸς οἰκοδομήν, ὡς ἔφην, τῶν λαῶν πάντα χρὴ πράττεσθαι παρ' ἡμῶν,
ἐπιτηρείτω ταῦτα ἡ θεοσέβεια ὑμῶν· καὶ εἰ μέλλοι τις χειροτονεῖσθαι κληρικός,
περιεργαζέσθω τὸν βίον αὐτοῦ, καὶ πότερόν ποτε γαμετὴν ἔχει ἢ οὔ, καὶ πῶς ἢ πότε
ἠγάγετο, καὶ εἰ ἀπέσχετο· καὶ εἰ μή τίς ἐστι τῶν ἐκβεβλημένων ἢ παρ' ἑτέρου
θεοσεβεστάτου ἐπισκόπου ἢ ἐκ μοναστηρίων· καὶ τότε χειροτονείτω, ἀδιάβλητον
εὑρεθέντα.
reviewer: claude (Wave A review, clause by clause against the Greek)
review_notes: Replaces a scaffold row ('Rem mid: …'); the section had no real English before Wave A.
Checked clause by clause against the Greek: 'ἐπιτηρείτω ταῦτα ἡ θεοσέβεια ὑμῶν' = 'let Your Reverence watch over these matters'.

Reviewer rv0 fixes applied before merge: agency kept with 'Your Reverence' for περιεργαζέσθω and χειροτονείτω (the draft had supplied 'the bishop'); plain indirect question for εἰ μή τίς ἐστι; 'abstained' for ἀπέσχετο; 'married her' for ἠγάγετο.
Scripture: ἀδιάβλητον εὑρεθέντα may recall 1 Timothy 3:10, but the wording differs (ἀνέγκλητοι there); uncertain, so no inline citation.
